She later competed on ''[[Big Brother 13 (US)]]'' and ''[[Big Brother 22 (US)]]''. Daniele first competed on ''Big Brother 8'', alongside her estranged father [[Dick Donato]], as a part of the rivals twist. She spent much of the season balancing the demands of the game with her tumultuous yet beneficial relationship with Dick. Despite being a frequent target due to the pair's visibility, Daniele emerged as one of the season's strongest competitors, winning 2 Head of Household and 5 Power of Veto competitions and helping her alliance survive repeated attacks from opposing factions. Alongside Dick, she navigated numerous power shifts, benefited from key strategic decisions by allies, and reached the Final Two after dominating the endgame. Although many respected her competitive success and resilience, the jury ultimately rewarded Dick's more assertive strategic game, and Daniele lost in a 5–2 vote, finishing as the runner-up. Daniele also returned for ''Big Brother 13'', where she was partnered with Dick once more. After Dick left the game, Daniele was given a [[Golden Key]], allowing her to stay safe until the final ten. Initially entering the house as a part of the [[Veterans|Veterans Alliance]], she attempted to save her newfound ally [[Dominic Briones]] by pitting the Veterans against each other, but with her plan backfiring and Dominic being eventually evicted, she eventually defected from this alliance to team up with newbies [[Porsche Briggs]] and [[Kalia Booker]]. She also had a season-long feud with ''[[Big Brother 12 (US)]]'' houseguest and eventual winner [[Rachel Reilly]]. Deemed as a massive threat by her former allies, she was [[Backdoor|backdoored]] by [[Jeff Schroeder]] despite the fact that they had a deal before, although [[Shelly Moore]] attempted to flip to save Daniele to go against Jeff and [[Jordan Lloyd]], [[Adam Poch]] betrayed the Newbies and decided to go with Jeff & Jordan, thus Daniele was evicted during the first half of the first [[Double Eviction]] by a vote of 3-2, placing 8th and becoming the second [[Jury|juror]]. In ''Big Brother 22'', Daniele was a key member of the dominant [[The Committee]] alliance and formed close relationships with fellow alliance members [[Nicole Franzel]] and [[Cody Calafiore]]. She also maintained a friendship with outsider [[Da'Vonne Rogers]]. After becoming the HoH in week 6, she targeted ally [[Tyler Crispen]] for throwing her under the bus the previous week after the disruptor power [[David Alexander]] from removed himself from the block. However, feeling anxious about her last appearance, Daniele decided to play it safe and patch things up with Tyler and nominated her former ally [[Ian Terry]] as the new target, This proved to be a fatal mistake as two weeks later during the triple eviction, she became the first victim when the Committee had to turn on themselves, as she was nominated by Tyler in the third round of the [[Triple Eviction]] against her ally Nicole. When both she and Nicole failed to win the veto, In an attempt to save herself, Dani called out Tyler and [[Christmas Abbott]] for having a final 2 alliance during the plea speeches. Despite this, she was evicted unanimously over Nicole in a 4-0 vote. She had a dislike towards [[David Alexander]], found quarrels with [[Kevin Campbell]] and a short-lived rivalry with [[Kaysar Ridha]], but was one of a few people to tolerate [[Janelle Pierzina]]. She placed 7th and became the fifth juror. Daniele is often considered one of the best physical competitors in the history of the show. Across all her three seasons, she won a total of 5 HOHs and 5 POVs, comprising the third most competition wins among multiple seasons.

She originally competed on ''[[Big Brother 16 (US)]]'' and later on ''[[Big Brother 22 (US)]]''. On ''Big Brother 16 (US)'', Nicole became best known for her showmance with [[Hayden Voss]], and her competition threat status, as she would win 3 [[Head of Household|Head of Households]] and 2 [[Battle of the Block|Battle of the Blocks]]. After losing allies [[Jocasta Odom]] and Hayden and during the first Double Eviction, Nicole was left on the bottom along with [[Donny Thompson]]. In Week 7, she managed to win HOH, but she was dethroned and later backstabbed by her friend [[Christine Brecht]], who nominated her against Donny, leading to Nicole's unanimous eviction. However, she managed to return to the game via winning the [[Re-Entry Competition]] one week later, and in Week 9, she was once again nominated against her ally Donny, before surviving eviction. In Week 10, she became a pawn against main target Christine, but despite Christine winning the [[Power of Veto]], [[Derrick Levasseur]] wanted to keep her, and HOH [[Caleb Reynolds]] wished to backdoor [[Frankie Grande]]. However, after Nicole told Derrick he reminded her of [[Dan Gheesling]], he decided to turn on her. He convinced Caleb not to backdoor Frankie, and Caleb nominated Nicole's last remaining ally, [[Victoria Rafaeli]] alongside her. Nicole was evicted for the second time by a 4-0 vote, placing 7th and becoming the 5th member of the [[jury]]. Nicole Franzel played a subtle, under-the-radar game on ''Big Brother 18 (US)'', joining the [[8-Pack]] alliance early and maintaining strong social connections while quietly influencing decisions behind the scenes. Her showmance with [[Corey Brooks]] helped keep her safe, and despite losing allies like [[Zakiyah Everette]] and [[Paulie Calafiore]], Nicole and Corey recovered by positioning themselves between the two sides of the house. After winning key competitions late in the game, Nicole helped eliminate major threats like [[Victor Arroyo]] and eventually survived the Final 4 eviction when [[Paul Abrahamian]] targeted her and Corey. Despite losing part 3 of the final HOH, she convinced Paul to take her to the final 2 over [[James Huling]]. Her behind the scenes gameplay, subtle persuasion, and the jury's distaste towards Paul's behavior won her the game in a close 5-4 vote, becoming the first female to defeat a male in the final 2. Despite entering ''Big Brother 22 (US)'' as one of two previous winners and forming a long-running feud with [[Janelle Pierzina]], Nicole would join the dominant [[The Committee]] alliance, which kept her safe alongside her strong allyship with [[Da'Vonne Rogers]] and [[Ian Terry]]. She was close with Committee members [[Daniele Briones|Dani Briones]] and fellow ''Big Brother 16 (US)'' castmate [[Cody Calafiore]], having final 2 deals with both. Despite her manipulative and eviction-contributing status, Nicole wouldn't face much heat until the [[Triple Eviction]], in which she was nominated in the second and third rounds before managing to survive. At the final 5, she won her first HOH and POV of the season, which were keys to evicting a major threat in Committee member [[Memphis Garrett]]. Despite being nominated as the target by [[Enzo Palumbo]] at the final 4, she was spared when Cody saved her and evicted [[Christmas Abbott]]. After losing the final Head of Household competition to Cody, she was blindsided and evicted by the latter, resulting in her finishing in 3rd place and becoming the 9th and final member of the jury. On ''Reindeer Games'', Nicole found herself in an uncertain position after discovering that both [[Britney Haynes]] and Cody Calafiore, who she had personal issues with, were also playing. Immediately, she quickly made amends with both, repairing her friendship with Britney while keeping an alliance of convenience with Cody, though she did not trust him this time. She flew under-the-radar for the majority of the game, due to her perceived low threat level, and formed key strong social bonds later with [[Frankie Grande]] and [[Taylor Hale]]. Though underestimated again by others, Nicole showed her prowess in winning key competitions, and narrowly defeated [[Josh Martinez]], and later [[Xavier Prather]] and Taylor at the finale to win the season, becoming the first two-time North American ''Big Brother'' winner. Across all four of her seasons, Nicole has won twice, placed 3rd once, placed 7th once, and has won 16 competitions total. Due to her high placements, amount of competition wins, and excellent social and strategic game across her seasons, she is often regarded as one of the best players in ''Big Brother'' history.
